title: Find the long-run limit of an exponential model to evaluate it
content: For a model of the form y = A - B e^(-kt) with k > 0, as t increases without bound the term e^(-kt) tends to 0, so y tends towards A. This value A is the model's long-run (limiting) value — e.g. the maximum sustainable temperature, population, or other modelled quantity. To evaluate whether the model is realistic or appropriate, compare this limiting value A to a known real-world figure (such as a stated boiling point or maximum capacity). If A is much smaller or much larger than the known figure, the model is not appropriate for describing behaviour beyond a certain point, and your conclusion should state this comparison explicitly rather than simply asserting 'good' or 'bad'.
